title: Phase-oscillation harness and stability protocol for throughput benchmarking
content:
Purpose:
This note documents a phase-oscillation style throughput harness and stability protocol aimed at producing repeatable throughput SLO estimates while surfacing subtle contention modes (KV-cache thrash, kernel scheduling collisions, inter-instance crosstalk). The approach emphasizes controlled, repeatable perturbations instead of long single-plateau runs to (1) shorten wall-clock experiment time, (2) expose non-linear system state changes, and (3) produce statistically robust confidence intervals for steady-state throughput.

Context / why different: 
We have many steady-state warmup playbooks in-drive. This doc introduces a purposely oscillatory load pattern (alternating low/medium/high phases) plus seeded trace replay and bootstrapped CI estimation. The oscillation both primes long-tail resources and reveals whether short bursts cause lingering degradation (e.g., allocator fragmentation, GPU kernel cache eviction).

Goals / success criteria:
- Produce median and 95% CI for stable throughput per model/config within a 90-minute experiment window.
- Detect persistent state shifts post-burst (recovery time) and produce a simple scalar recovery_time_s.
- Maintain repeatability across runs (stdev < 3% for median throughput across N=5 independent runs).

High-level harness design:
- Phase-based pattern: repeat N cycles of {settle, ramp, burst, settle} rather than single steady plateau. Typical cycle: 60s settle (low QPS), 120s ramp (linear increase to target), 60s burst (target QPS sustained), 120s settle (low QPS).
- Seeded requests: use a deterministic request sequence file (JSONL) with fixed prompts, deterministic tokenizer split, and precomputed sequence-length histogram. Replay mode must preserve ordering and inter-arrival jitter seed.
- Warmup seeding: a short dedicated priming pass of model-specific KV-prefixes to populate cache for common prefixes before measurement begins.
- Telemetry alignment: all samples tagged with an experiment_id and phase_id. Keep monotonic timestamp in ISO format and monotonic sample index.

Load generator configuration knobs (example key/value pairs to stash in harness configs):
- target_qps: 1200  # desired QPS for burst phase
- threads_per_client: 8
- ramp_seconds: 120
- burst_seconds: 60
- settle_qps: 10
- num_cycles: 6
- seed: 1337  # RNG seed for inter-arrival jitter and sample ordering
- request_trace: traces/llm-summaries-10k.jsonl
- max_concurrency_per_client: 32
- client_backpressure_policy: reject|queue (recommend queue with bounded depth=100)
- token_inflight_shaping: true  # experimental; shape QPS by token emission budget

Practical example harness command (pseudo-shell):
- export EXP=osc-20240930-aisha
- ./bench-runner --config configs/oscillation.json --trace traces/llm-summaries-10k.jsonl --seed 1337 --outdir artifacts/$EXP

Key metrics to capture per-sample (minimum):
- request_id (string), experiment_id, phase_id, timestamp_iso, sample_index
- qps_reported_by_client, latency_p99_ms, latency_p50_ms, latency_p90_ms, tokens_out, tokens_in, model_variant, instance_id
- gpu_util_pct, gpu_memory_mb, cuda_kernel_time_ms (from perf counters), host_cpu_pct, net_rx_bytes, net_tx_bytes
- kv_cache_hit_ratio, kv_cache_entries, kv_cache_eviction_count

Analysis & repeatability recipe:
1) Per-cycle trimming: for each cycle keep only the middle 40% of the burst period to reduce edge effects from ramp/settle transitions.
2) Aggregate per-cycle medians and compute bootstrap 95% CI across cycles (B=2000 resamples). This gives CI that accounts for cross-cycle variance.
3) Repeat the entire experiment 5 independent times (different process start, same seed) and compute run-to-run variance. Expectation: median throughput stdev < 3%. If > 6% investigate non-determinism sources (network, scheduler, autoscaler).
4) Recovery detection: after each burst, compute 1-min sliding mean of latency and tokens/sec; recovery_time_s is the time until sliding mean returns within 5% of pre-burst baseline for two consecutive windows.

Profiling hooks and artifacts to collect:
- Lightweight: client request log (compressed JSONL), server request logs with phase tags, model-level perf counters (per-request kernel time), and Prometheus metrics scrape (1s resolution) during run.
- Deep profile (selected runs): GPU nvprof/cupti kernel timelines, host perf events (cycles, context switches), pprof of runtime thread stacks.
- Save system snapshots before/after run: nvidia-smi topo, dpkg --list (or rpm query), CUDA version, driver version, kernel, docker image digest.

Detection of non-linearities we care about:
- Throughput hysteresis: burst causes steady throughput next cycle to be lower despite identical QPS target.
- KV-cache thrash: kv_cache_eviction_count spikes correlate with latency tail inflation.
- Cross-instance crosstalk: when co-located instances show synchronous latency tail spikes during host-level GC or docker activity.

Quick checklist for running an experiment:
- [ ] Lock cluster autoscaler / disable scaling during run
- [ ] Ensure other noisy tenants removed from host (or run on dedicated nodes)
- [ ] Push trace and config to artifacts storage and pin git commit for bench-runner
- [ ] Clear KV-cache between independent runs if experiment aims to measure cold-start characteristics
- [ ] Start Prometheus scrape and ensure liveness of exporters
- [ ] Run 1 sanity short cycle (2 cycles) to validate instrumentation
- [ ] Run full N-cycle experiment (num_cycles=config.num_cycles) x repeats

Expected timings / sizing guidance:
- Small model (<6B): target end-to-end experiment time ~ 45–60 minutes for num_cycles=6 and 5 repeats.
- Medium model (6B–30B): 60–120 minutes.
- Large model (>30B): expect 2–4 hours for stable estimates unless you reduce cycles.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- High run-to-run variance: check for background cronjobs, frequency governors, container cpuset throttling. Consider pinning IRQs and CPU sets.
- Slow recovery after burst: inspect allocator fragmentation; recommend short process restarts between independent runs for isolating memory-leak-like effects.
- Non-repeatable traces due to non-deterministic tokenization: pre-tokenize trace and store integer token sequences.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Evaluate token_inflight_shaping (experimental) across model families and GPU architectures; add a toggle to harness and track impact on p95 latency.
- Define golden trace set per model family (small/medium/large) and publish under traces/golden/.
- Automated regression alerting: wire bootstrapped CI comparison to Optimize so that a regression >5% triggers a regression ticket.

Appendix: minimal JSONL trace sample (pre-tokenized, one per line):
{"id":"req-0001","tokens_in":12,"tokens_out_max":128,"prompt_hash":"abc123","text":"Summarize: ..."}
{"id":"req-0002","tokens_in":7,"tokens_out_max":64,"prompt_hash":"def456","text":"Write a short email about..."}

Notes to self: run pilot with 3 cycles on staging-gpu-1, check kernel eviction counters around cycle 2. If eviction_count > 1000, capture nvprof.

References / Related docs: CONFLUENCE-RT-987 (throughput methodology), bench-harness variants in drive (see linked PR).
